title: Now Streaming
details: Enter the arena's first live wave window.
directorFlavor: The cameras are on and you have not immediately embarrassed the production team. This is the minimum viable broadcast.

title: Warm-Up Act
details: Survive long enough for the arena to produce a modest audience count.
directorFlavor: Ten arena nuisances have made their contractual entrance and are no longer available for interviews. The Director calls this an opening number because it is too early to be impressed.

title: Name on the Marquee
popupText: New achievement: Name on the Marquee!
details: Reach the first act's headline presentation.
directorFlavor: The first Headliner has arrived and the arena has upgraded from crowd control to programming. Try not to make the marquee spell your name as a warning.

title: Backstage Pass
unlockCriteria: Reach the first Floor 4 Green Room visit.
details: Complete an act and enter the untimed sponsor break.
directorFlavor: You have reached the Green Room, where the violence pauses and the prices become aggressive. Please enjoy this commercial break before the arena remembers your name.

title: First Segment Wrapped
details: Reach the first intermission with the Headliner segment resolved.
directorFlavor: Act One has been wrapped, which is producer language for nobody important died on schedule. The crew is already resetting the arena while pretending this was always the plan.

title: Prime-Time Problem
details: Keep the arena schedule moving through its opening act.
directorFlavor: Four waves have entered the schedule and none of them requested a reshoot. The ratings department has upgraded your survival from novelty to usable footage. A junior editor has been assigned to find your flattering angle. This is considered a deeply avoidable expense.

title: Crowd Work
details: Handle a substantial live arena roster.
directorFlavor: Fifty bodies have been booked into the venue and you are still occupying the center of the shot. The audience cannot tell whether this is skill or a refusal to read the evacuation signage. Camera three has developed a nervous tremor. Production calls that immersive engagement.

title: Second Billing
details: Reach the second act's headline presentation.
directorFlavor: A second Headliner has accepted the booking, which means the first one did not scare production into canceling. Your continued employment is becoming an inconveniently compelling subplot. The marquee has started reserving space for apologies. Do not mistake typography for mercy.

title: Break-Room Regular
unlockCriteria: Reach two Floor 4 Green Room visits.
details: Use the arena's first two commercial breaks.
directorFlavor: You have visited the Green Room twice, proving that the curtain is not an elaborate trap door. The sponsors are delighted to see a returning customer and have adjusted nothing in your favor. A vendor recognizes your footsteps. Their welcome is priced separately.

title: Two Segments Deep
details: Survive the first two timed arena segments.
directorFlavor: Two acts are complete and the arena has stopped pretending the difficulty curve is a gentle suggestion. Production has moved your emergency contact from pencil to permanent marker. The next segment has been labeled educational. Education is rarely kind here.

title: Gold in the Edit
popupText: New achievement: Gold in the Edit!
unlockCriteria: Earn at least 18 gold from Floor 4 act income.
details: Accumulate the opening arena segment's first useful sponsor budget.
directorFlavor: The ledger has recorded eighteen pieces of arena-earned gold and not one was labeled sympathy. The sponsors will now call your earnings a storyline instead of an accounting error. Spend it or save it; the cameras only care that you made it. Accounting has reluctantly become a spectator sport.

title: Opening Marathon
details: Complete the full wave schedule of an opening act.
directorFlavor: Eight waves have crossed the threshold and the arena still has enough floor visible for camera operators to panic on it. The Director has filed your stamina under marketable assets. A sponsor has requested a branded water break. The arena has denied it on dramatic grounds.

title: Midcard Survivor
details: Reach the third act's headline presentation.
directorFlavor: Three Headliners have taken their turn at the spotlight and the spotlight has not yet been declared a hazard. The midcard is where careers go to become contractual obligations, so congratulations on the promotion. The booking office has begun whispering. Whispering is how it budgets panic.

title: Three-Break Tour
unlockCriteria: Reach three Floor 4 Green Room visits.
details: Use three commercial breaks between arena acts.
directorFlavor: The Green Room has seen you three times and is beginning to recognize your footsteps. Its vendors are practicing your name, mostly so they can put it on an invoice. The complimentary chairs now lean away from you. Furniture has instincts too.

title: Waves on Waves
details: Keep the broadcast schedule alive into the middle acts.
directorFlavor: Twelve waves have been released, which is enough content for a season recap and an uncomfortable number of sponsor bumpers. You continue to provide both, so production has stopped asking whether you understand the format. The recap narrator has lost their voice. Your schedule remains offensively healthy.

title: Midshow Roster
details: Carry the broadcast through its middle-act roster.
directorFlavor: Seventy-five extras have filled the arena and the camera still finds you on the first try. This is no longer crowd work; it is a staffing crisis with choreography. The Director has asked Facilities whether the floor comes with a warranty. Facilities has sent a waiver instead. It has your name already misspelled.

title: Middle Management
unlockCriteria: Earn at least 40 gold from Floor 4 act income.
details: Accumulate a working arena total through the first two acts.
directorFlavor: Forty pieces of arena income have reached the act ledger. You are now generating a budget in the middle of a siege, which is exactly the sort of promotion nobody should accept. The sponsors have prepared a larger invoice and a smaller smile. Your total has become a lower-third graphic. It remains informative even after you spend it.

title: Nearly Main Event
details: Reach the final act's Green Room break.
directorFlavor: Four acts are wrapped and the arena is down to its final excuse for being built. Your build has survived long enough that the Director is reviewing the finale notes with genuine, measurable concern. The finale crew has removed the word inevitable. They replaced it with expensive. The surviving stagehands are taking bets. None of them favor the building. The camera rig is aimed at the exits. This is not encouraging.

title: Headliner Hunter
details: Claim two headline encounters in the arena.
directorFlavor: Two Headliners have been removed from the running and their entrance music is now being used to fill dead air. Production wanted a rivalry; you supplied a cancellation notice with excellent timing. The audience is beginning to understand that the headline act is not always the person wearing the expensive costume. The Director is revising the booking sheet and quietly removing the word 'favorite.' Their agents have requested a softer replay. The replay department has sent back a louder one. This is what negotiations look like when everyone has claws. Keep collecting cancellations; the network loves a pattern.

title: Arena Veteran
unlockCriteria: Spawn one hundred Floor 4 arena enemies.
details: Remain in the broadcast through a full mid-floor roster.
directorFlavor: One hundred arena enemies have been assigned to your segment and the set is still technically standing. The camera crew has stopped counting entrances because your refusal to leave is easier to track. Every surviving extra has learned your movement pattern, which is unfortunate for them and educational for you. The Director has ordered a commemorative tally mark and billed it to audience development. The tally has required a second wall. Facilities calls this an architectural achievement. You call it Tuesday. The audience calls it a reason to keep watching.

title: Fourth Billing
details: Reach the fourth act's headline presentation.
directorFlavor: Four Headliners have entered the arena and the booking office has run out of polite ways to ask you to lose. The main-event roster is now watching you with professional interest. Their contracts describe this as entertainment; the contracts are lying. The Director has upgraded your threat assessment from contestant to recurring production problem. The remaining Headliner has asked for a larger entrance. Production offered them a larger liability waiver. The crowd applauded the paperwork. It was their wisest decision all night.

title: The Expensive Break
unlockCriteria: Reach four Floor 4 Green Room visits.
details: Enter the final commercial break before the Winner's Circle.
directorFlavor: Four Green Room visits have turned hospitality into a recurring expense report. The tables keep rerolling, the prices keep climbing, and you keep returning with enough life left to shop. Sponsors call this customer loyalty; the arena calls it a countdown. The Director calls it a scheduling inconvenience with excellent retention. Your usual table has been roped off for safety. The rope is decorative and deeply insulting. Please browse quickly; the next act is already warming up. Your receipt now has its own segment. It is performing terribly.

title: Bought the Extra Minute
popupText: New achievement: Bought the Extra Minute!
details: Survive long enough for a Headliner fight to exceed its scheduled window.
directorFlavor: The Headliner refused to leave, so the network bought an extra minute and called it premium content. You are still fighting inside the overrun, which is either admirable or a serious misunderstanding of labor law. The arena clock has become a threat with numerals. Production is charging the audience for every second you make them watch. The Director is pleased to discover that panic has a billing code. A sponsor has purchased the blinking red timer. Their slogan is somehow less comforting than the alarm. The overtime crew has entered wearing helmets. They insist the helmets are purely ceremonial.

title: Four-Act Purse
unlockCriteria: Earn at least 75 gold from Floor 4 act income.
details: Accumulate enough arena income to document late-floor earnings.
directorFlavor: Seventy-five pieces of arena-earned gold now appear in your ledger, each one carrying the faint smell of a sponsor's regret. You have converted escalating danger into a budget and then survived long enough to use it. The vendors are thrilled; the enemies are less so. The Director has marked your economy as a second weapon and assigned it a camera angle. The total is historical, not protected from your shopping habits. History is the only asset production cannot repossess. Keep making it expensive. The cash counter is smoking. The finance team insists this is normal.

title: Co-Star Contract
unlockCriteria: Host a carried Companion co-star on Floor 4.
details: Bring a completed Floor 3 Companion contract into the arena.
directorFlavor: A Companion has joined the arena and production must now account for a second set of heroics. The contract says co-star; the footage says emergency management with better posture. The Headliners did not budget for teamwork. The Director has reluctantly expanded the shot list and is already pricing matching merchandise. Two names now appear on the survival graphic. The graphic is visibly sweating. Continue being inconveniently cooperative; it ruins the solo-collapse montage. The editors are forced to learn a second name. They resent your friendship professionally.

title: Final Billing
details: Clear every Headliner encounter before the final exit.
directorFlavor: Five Headliners have taken the stage and five have been removed from the schedule. The arena has become a very expensive lesson in refusing to be impressed. Their entrance announcements are now archival material. The audience expected a finale and received a complete staffing reduction. Production has run out of replacement bosses, which is the closest thing this floor has to an apology. The Director is checking whether the Winner's Circle has a vacancy for you or merely another trap. Every dressing room is empty. Every manager is suddenly unavailable. The merchandise team has crossed out five faces and circled yours in red. This is not a promotion. It is a containment strategy. Walk carefully; the confetti budget may still be armed.

title: Five Acts, No Notes
popupText: New achievement: Five Acts, No Notes!
details: Reach the fifth Green Room and finish the full timed program.
directorFlavor: All five acts are complete and the arena has delivered its entire authored program without a mercy edit. You survived every schedule, every escalation, and every Headliner booking. The Green Room is now a Winner's Circle because language is cheaper than construction. The audience is on its feet, mostly because the seats have been removed for cleanup. Production has filed your run under 'unexpectedly reusable footage.' The Director has no notes, which is not the same as approval but is considerably rarer. Take the exit before somebody invents a sixth act. The stage manager has begun dismantling the danger signs. They leave the largest one pointed at you. It says season renewal pending. Please do not read that as a threat. It is definitely a threat.

title: The Main Event
unlockCriteria: Clear Floor 4 and confirm the Winner's Circle exit.
details: Complete the five-act broadcast and leave through the terminal Green Room.
directorFlavor: The Main Event has ended with you standing in the Winner's Circle and the arena unable to schedule another problem. Five acts, five Headliners, one contestant who declined every obvious exit opportunity. The cameras found their closing shot and the sponsors found a new adjective for your survival. The audience wanted a collapse and got a completed program instead. The Director is forced to admit the format worked exactly as intended, which is humiliating for everyone involved. Floor 5 is waiting with a different kind of paperwork. Please leave before the set changes its mind. The exit stairs have been polished for the first time this season. A production assistant is crying into the confetti. The ratings are excellent. Their future is less certain. Congratulations on becoming the evidence.

title: Clean Broadcast
details: Defeat every Headliner within its scheduled headline window.
directorFlavor: The broadcast reached its finale without buying a single extra minute. Every Headliner left on schedule, every act stayed inside its slot, and production did not have to invent a premium cut called 'The Clock Ate Us.' The audience received a clean escalation instead of a delay notice. The crew is furious because competence has ruined three emergency segments. The Director has reviewed the timeline twice and found no useful disaster. This is not luck; it is an aggressively maintained margin. The Winner's Circle is open, and for once nobody is shouting about overtime. The clock crew has packed up its emergency siren. They are taking it personally. A sponsor has demanded a refund on suspense. The Director has denied it with unusual joy. Efficient survival is still survival, regrettably.

title: Season Purse
unlockCriteria: Earn at least 160 gold from Floor 4 act income.
details: Finish the arena program with substantial cumulative earnings.
directorFlavor: One hundred sixty pieces of arena-earned gold have been recorded across five acts. The economy segment has become a second finale, complete with escalating stakes and no competent accountant. Sponsors are calling your cumulative earnings an investment while quietly checking whether they can be repossessed. The audience expected a survival story and got a budget report with explosions. Production has added a cash-counting camera to the Winner's Circle. The Director approves of any contestant who turns danger into liquidity. Spend it wisely, or at least spend it where the cameras can see. The ledger has become required viewing. The vendors have started offering commemorative receipts. Each receipt is longer than a Headliner's contract. Your earnings survived the story even if your balance did not. That is the sort of fiscal drama this show can monetize.
